name: Christensen Hall
use: First-year residence hall (ten floors) beside Philbrook Dining Hall; twin of Williamson
builtText: Opened September 1969, completed late 1969; dedicated September 19, 1970
architect: Ulrich Franzen & Associates (builder: Harvey Construction Co.)

renovations.what: Planned renovation with Williamson (interiors, bathrooms, common areas, heating and plumbing); $32.3M of deferred maintenance addressed. Design/construction status not confirmed.

facts.text: Designed by Ulrich Franzen & Associates and built by Harvey Construction, it was UNH's second high-rise residence; it opened to residents in September 1969 and was dedicated September 19, 1970.
It was the first UNH hall with an apartment for a faculty member in residence, meant to foster student-faculty contact outside class.
Named for Ernest W. Christensen, a 1923 graduate, coach and trustee (1940-61).

Housing describes small floor communities of 25-35 residents, a first-floor study lounge with fireplace, a basement rec lounge (52-inch TV, pool, ping-pong, foosball, piano), outdoor athletic courts and picnic area; floor plans list ten floors.
Accessibility per Housing: braille signage, elevator, roll-in building access, strobe/audible alerts in all rooms. No air conditioning listed.

UNH Facilities lists a Williamson & Christensen renovation: at 50 years old the interiors are worn, bathrooms and common spaces need modernizing, and heating and plumbing systems are failing; the project addresses $32.3 million in deferred maintenance.

verdict: Ulrich Franzen's stepped brick tower, bold from outside but worn within: no A/C, dated baths, renovation pending.
notes: No licensed photo of Christensen found on Commons (only Williamson). Reference photos show deep red-brick towers with recessed, stepped window bays and a brick-lined undercroft entrance (the old row's "concrete towers" is wrong: cladding is brick). Room photo: painted walls, average ceiling, one window. Cost: search snippets cite a $70M state-committee approval (Jan 2026) and a USNH not-to-exceed of $76M (Dec 2025), but I could not open either source (scanned PDF / 404), so no cost is recorded. Old row's DOCOMOMO-US and Buildings of New England claims not verified. Hall size not stated on the Christensen page; Society19 dates are page publish dates (content appears older).
judgeNotes: Reference photos show sculpted brick towers with recessed bays (not concrete as the old run said). Character down a point: Franzen design is notable, but the story is thin. The planned 2026 renovation is marked major: false until it is done.
